description:
FILED s465az (Opus, round 23, phase 0 of the ignored-tests audit #993).

THE CAP: tools/run-perl-suite.pl's per-test failure log stops after 500
diverging rows per file (run_one, the `last if ++$rows >= 500` that is now a
splice).  That cap predates the row baseline and was INVISIBLE: the log simply
ended, and nothing said it had.

WHAT IT COSTS NOW: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv (I1) is built from that log,
so for a file over the cap the blessed multiset is PARTIAL and a NEW failing
row past position 500 cannot be seen.  Measured on the s465az `--all` run,
19 files exceed it:

  comp/require.t  comp/utf.t  io/crlf_through.t  op/write.t  opbasic/cmp.t
  re/charset.t  re/pat.t  re/pat_advanced.t  re/reg_posixcc.t
  re/regex_sets_compat.t  re/regexp.t  re/regexp_noamp.t  re/regexp_notrie.t
  re/regexp_qr.t  re/regexp_qr_embed.t  re/regexp_trielist.t  uni/fold.t
  uni/upper.t  uni/variables.t

The log now writes `# TRUNCATED: N diverging row(s), only the first 500 are
listed` as a COMMENT (every reader skips comments, so the #185 expected-rows
multisets are byte-identical to before) and every report counts these files.
So the hole is COUNTED, not silent â which is the standard this project holds
a hole to â but it is still a hole.

WHAT TO DECIDE (do not just raise the cap):
  1. Raising it changes what `diverging_rowkeys` returns for these files, which
     changes the #185 expected-rows verdicts for any registered member.  Any
     change must diff the XDIFF/STALE verdicts of all 111 registered files
     before and after.
  2. re/reg_posixcc.t is the extreme case and a separate anomaly already noted
     in docs/plan-test-audit-s464.md Â§2d: PCL produces 9,190 TAP rows against
     perl's 2,560, so its "diverging rows" are mostly a row-count artefact.
     Its cap should probably follow that investigation, not lead it.
  3. A cheaper option than a bigger cap: key the truncated files' baselines on
     a per-file DIGEST of the whole diverging multiset plus the first 500 rows,
     so a change past the cap moves the digest even though the rows are not
     listed.  Costs one line per file and keeps the file readable.

RELATED: #993 (the audit), docs/plan-test-audit-s464.md Â§3 I1,
docs/test-debugging-runbook.md Â§4d.


=== s469bf (2026-09-05, Opus) — the cap is not only a HOLE, it is a NOISE SOURCE ===

Measured while attributing the s468 companion ROW DIFF.  A truncated file writes
exactly 500 PAIRED diverging rows (extras are appended after the cap and do not
consume the window), so the window's right edge is a function of how many rows
diverged BEFORE it.  Put a volatile block early in such a file and every row at
the right edge becomes NEW/FIXED noise although nothing about it changed:

  re/pat.t           volatile block at perl rows 277-292 (`for (keys %ans)`);
                     last paired row 718 -> 722 between two runs of ONE tree,
                     carrying four `(?il), utf8=…, locale=…` rows in and out.
  re/pat_advanced.t  volatile block at rows 29-36 (`each %d`);
                     last paired row 1186 -> 1189, carrying three `((?^:\v))`
                     rows in and out.

That is why both files had to be registered `*rows-unstable*` WHOLE (task
#1082, s469bf) rather than having their dozen genuinely volatile rows
normalised: the cap propagates one block's volatility to the whole tail.

So option 3 in this task (a per-file DIGEST of the full multiset beside the
first 500 rows) would NOT help these two — the digest would move on every draw
for the same reason.  What would: a bigger cap does not remove the volatility
but does stop it from MOVING the boundary, since the boundary would no longer
exist for these files (re/pat.t 1045 diverging rows, re/pat_advanced.t ~520,
comp/require.t 1747-ish).  Both remain behind this task's rule: diff the
XDIFF/STALE verdicts of all 111 registered files before and after.

ALSO MEASURED HERE: the cap is what makes comp/require.t's real count move
(909/835 -> 906/836 -> 910/837 across s396 / s440 / s465az+) unattributable at
the row level — its first 500 diverging rows are byte-identical in every run, so
the three rows that actually changed are past the boundary and invisible.
subject: The companion ROW baseline (I1) is PARTIAL for the 19 files whose per-test failure log hits the 500-row cap â the truncation is now announced and counted, but a NEW failing row past row 500 is still invisible
